jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.excerpt: About The Company goop is a lifestyle platform dedicated to exploration, curation, and groundbreaking conversation.
jobs.description:
About The Company

goop is a lifestyle platform dedicated to exploration, curation, and groundbreaking conversation. From its award-winning beauty and fashion lines to its expansive editorial lens, goop invites women to embrace the process of becoming, and to discover deep joy in the pursuit of pleasure, beauty, and growth in all phases of life.

Gwyneth Paltrow began goop in the fall of 2008 as a weekly newsletter. It has expanded into a beauty, fashion, and food business that’s also known for its products, curation, podcast, TV shows, live events, and retail stores.

About You

You operate in founder mode: high agency, high EQ, and razor-sharp instincts. You read the room quickly, sense what's needed before you're asked, and move on it. You are a thoughtful and proactive strategic partner who excels at aligning teams, priorities, and communication — equally comfortable zooming out to understand company-wide operations and strategy, and diving in to drive execution on critical initiatives.

This role represents the Co-CEOs' interests across three worlds: goop's business (beauty & fashion), Gwyneth's media presence, and investment interests. You move fluidly between them, often within the same day.

You are AI-first and AI-native. You don't wait for someone else to build the tool — you build it yourself: standing up Notion dashboards, wiring together plugins and AI agents, and turning no-code experiments into real operational workflows for the Co-CEOs and executive team. With strong communication instincts and sound judgment, you navigate senior stakeholders with confidence and help ensure clarity, alignment, and momentum across the organization.

Who You Are

  • Founder-mode operator — high agency and an ability to act on instinct, before being asked
  • Context-switcher — comfortable moving between all three worlds in the same day
  • Exceptional communicator — confident and clear across formats and audiences
  • Operational powerhouse — you drive structure, efficiency, and accountability in fast-moving, complex environments
  • Sharp writer and researcher — you produce clean, efficient memos, updates, and diligence work that get straight to the point, no fluff
  • Highly collaborative with a good sense of humor — you stay warm, steady, and easy to work with under pressure
  • Highly trustworthy and discreet — you'll handle sensitive information and critical relationships
  • Action-oriented leader — you don't just advise; you own and drive results

How You Operate

  • You operate in full alignment with the Co-CEOs' thinking — when you speak on their behalf, you speak with clarity and conviction, and you recalibrate fast when something's off
  • You extend the Co-CEOs' reach: proactively managing every relationship that matters
  • You communicate early and often — proactive updates are the default, not the exception
  • You're warm and honest — you handle direct communication well and don't avoid hard conversations
  • You assume good intent and offer people the benefit of the doubt — and expect the same in return
  • You understand that small gestures, done right, build long-term trust and relationship equity

About the Role

The Chief of Staff will serve as a strategic partner to goop's Co-CEOs and executive team, driving strategic alignment, execution, and communication across the organization. This role reports directly to the Co-CEOs, representing their interests across three worlds: goop's business (beauty & fashion), Gwyneth's media presence, and investment interests — working across time zones with global, cross-functional teams. The Chief of Staff must be able to shift context across these worlds multiple times in a single day without losing focus or dropping a thread, and ensures the Co-CEOs' priorities are clearly translated into action across each of them — supporting effective executive operations and helping shape company-wide operations, communication, and culture — while owning a high volume of board, portfolio, and investment work across the business.

CO-CEO PARTNERSHIP & STRATEGIC SUPPORT

  • Ensure the Co-CEOs' priorities are clearly communicated across the organization and support the Co-CEOs in driving execution by direct reports and cross-functional teams
  • Act as gatekeeper — knowing when to filter and when to let things flow directly — and, as requested by the Co-CEOs, serve as proxy in key meetings, synthesizing, summarizing, and relaying critical insights to inform decision-making
  • Field, review, prioritize, and, where appropriate, respond to incoming requests, proposals, and opportunities directed to the Co-CEOs
  • Work closely with the Co-CEOs' Executive Assistant(s) to communicate and sequence priorities, manage scheduling trade-offs, and optimize the Co-CEOs' time and focus — across time zones as needed
  • Prepare executive-ready briefings, memos, and presentations — equipping the Co-CEOs with the context, data, and materials needed for internal, board, and external engagements
  • Shape how the Co-CEOs represent the company's strategy and brand to internal teams, the board, media, and external partners
  • Collaborate with the social media team to execute the Co-CEOs' personal social presence across channels, ensuring authenticity, alignment with brand values, and consistency with their voice
  • Partner with the Head of Communications to prepare the Co-CEOs for media appearances and public engagements — building background materials, researching attendees and guests, and managing protocol
  • Coordination with podcast production team, as needed

AI-ENABLED OPERATIONS & SYSTEMS

  • Design, build, and maintain AI-driven systems — including a Co-CEO-facing Notion dashboard layered with plugins and AI agents — serving as the single source of truth for real-time visibility into priorities, decisions, and follow-ups across all three worlds
  • Continuously explore and test new AI tools, plugins, and agents, turning promising ones into practical, repeatable workflows for the Co-CEOs and executive team
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to spot operational bottlenecks and solve them with AI-driven automation and internal tooling
  • Monitor the performance of AI-driven workflows and iterate for continual improvement
  • Build documentation and best practices for AI-enabled operations so tools and workflows scale and transfer beyond any one person

EXECUTIVE TEAM LEADERSHIP & STRATEGIC OPERATIONS

  • Lead and facilitate weekly executive team meetings, including setting clear agendas, driving accountability, and ensuring timely follow-through on action items
  • Meet regularly with senior subject-matter leaders to align on priorities, share Co-CEO context, and ensure cross-functional clarity and collaboration
  • Serve as a trusted strategic partner to every department head — not just the C-suite — translating the Co-CEOs' priorities into function-specific plans and holding cross-functional teams accountable to them
  • Facilitate alignment and communication between the Co-CEOs and direct reports to accelerate decision-making and maintain organizational focus
  • Partner with executive leaders to develop OKRs and track execution against strategic priorities
  • Act as lead strategic project manager on key cross-functional initiatives, ensuring clear ownership, timelines, and outcomes
  • When requested by the Co-CEOs or other executives, contribute to strategic discussions by providing context and insights that reflect Co-CEO and company priorities
  • Capture notes and action items during board and offsite sessions; track follow-ups and ensure accountability across functional leaders
  • Own ambiguous, high-priority special projects that don't have a clear owner — from research sprints to one-off initiatives — and see them through to completion

COMPANY-WIDE COMMUNICATION & CULTURE

  • Shape Co-CEO-led communications for all-company meetings and standups, ensuring alignment with the company's values, strategy, and priorities
  • Partner with the People team to develop monthly standup agendas, coordinating with functional leaders to highlight key initiatives and ensure diverse team representation
  • Partner cross-functionally to source, edit, and align content for company-wide meetings — overseeing slide development and deck design to ensure clarity, consistency, and on-brand voice
  • Prepare the Co-CEOs' talking points and visual aids to support effective delivery and high employee engagement
  • Coordinate logistics and production details to ensure seamless execution of company-wide meetings and events

BOARD, PORTFOLIO & INVESTMENT SUPPORT

  • Drive preparation and execution for quarterly board meetings, including cross-functional coordination for content collection, synthesis, and development of board-ready materials
  • Own end-to-end development of board decks, board presentations, and corporate executive presentations — content, synthesis, and design — ensuring materials are polished and aligned with strategic priorities across goop and goop beauty
  • Build and manage corporate agendas across the business, from executive offsites to board sessions to company-wide meetings
  • Partner with the Co-CEOs and executive team to ensure board discussions and materials are aligned with key strategic priorities and business performance
  • Design and execute off-site retreats — from agenda architecture that balances strategic discussion, business planning, and team-building, to logistics and follow-through on action items
  • Support portfolio management and investment-related workstreams — tracking opportunities, coordinating diligence, and keeping materials current across goop, goop beauty, and Gwyneth's broader investment activities
  • Partner closely with Corporate Development on deal flow, diligence, and new investment or partnership opportunities
  • Collaborate with the Co-CEOs' Executive Assistant(s) on logistics and scheduling, while leading content flow, sequencing, and communication of expectations to the executive tea.
  • Coordinate cross-functional contributors and external facilitators to deliver impactful sessions that advance company goals

CROSS-PORTFOLIO RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT

  • Manage the CRM and contact records — keeping them accurate, deduplicated, and consistently structured (you don't need to build the CRM, but you own how well it runs)
  • Track engagement and relationship health across investors, board members, founders, and key partners — flagging relationships before they go cold
  • Run periodic audits across relationships and initiatives to surface what needs re-engagement, escalation, or a decision from the Co-CEOs
  • Act as the connective tissue across Gwyneth's world — the person who always knows what's happening across all three worlds, and can brief the Co-CEOs on any of them at a moment's notice

Qualifications & Experience

Experience: 3–5 years of business experience, at least 2 years working directly with C-level executives; experience with consumer goods strongly preferred.

Leadership: Proven ability to drive executive programs and high-level strategic initiatives cross-functionally.

Technical Skills: Strong experience with Microsoft suite and data analytics tools. AI-native and fluent with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Notion, Asana, G-Suite, and Airtable, with hands-on experience building and maintaining Notion boards, databases, dashboards, plugins, AI agents, and no-code automations (e.g., Zapier). Experience managing CRM systems and contact records (accuracy, deduplication, structure).

Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business required.

Skills: Strong analytical capabilities, financial acumen, and the ability to succeed in a dynamic environment. Comfortable with direct communication, ambiguity, and rapid iteration, and experienced working across time zones with global, cross-functional teams.

FAQ

Goop, in good faith, reasonably expects to pay the position within this salary range. Goop provides the salary range in compliance with all applicable federal, state and local laws. The actual base salary will depend on numerous factors such as: experience, training, knowledge and skills, and if the location of the job changes.

jobs.excerpt: About UsTemporal is an open source programming model that can simplify code, make applications more reliable, and help developers focus on the important things like delivering features faster.
jobs.description:
About Us

Temporal is an open source programming model that can simplify code, make applications more reliable, and help developers focus on the important things like delivering features faster. We are on a mission to be the reliable foundation of every developer’s toolbox, and are building the team that will make that happen.
Our values guide us —they are present in how we show up, make decisions, and work together to make an impact. We’re curious, driven, collaborative, genuine and humble.
Temporal is growing and we are looking for those who share our values, challenge 'standard' thinking, and want to influence our future. If you have a passion for improving the developer experience, building world-class open-source software and communities, and want to be a part of our amazing team, we'd love to hear from you!

Summary

We have an opening to hire a Software Engineer, AI Foundations.

Temporal provides a reliable foundation powering AI leaders such as OpenAI, NVIDIA, Cursor, Lovable, Replit, and others. Its adoption is also expanding to users spanning across a broad range of AI applications. These range from agents to data pipelines and everything in between.

The mission of the AI Foundations team is to accelerate Temporal adoption across the entire ecosystem. Our approach combines a deep understanding of use cases with technical principles such as computer systems and software design fundamentals.

If you thrive on blending theory and practice, then this is the right team for you. We are an action-oriented group that loves to ship fast and solve customer problems. We also seek thorough technical grounding for our work and invest in systems and practices that foster long-term success.

Agentic development is a huge focus. We maintain a set of agents skills that give Codex, Claude Code, and similar tools a major boost when writing Temporal applications. These are already unblocking a large backlog of projects among our customer base. They also are an extraordinary point of leverage for Temporal’s mission, which has always been about accelerating developers as they build and operate reliable software. Working in this area puts you at the forefront of the agentic coding revolution.

Another major area of investment is our partner ecosystem. We developed a plugin system that makes it easy to add Temporal’s durable execution to popular open source agent frameworks such as Pydantic AI, AI SDK by Vercel, Google ADK, OpenAI Agents SDK, and others. Getting these abstractions right involves both creativity and critical trade-off analysis. Many challenges of this flavor remain to be solved. As we make progress, we instill our learnings in our internal AI systems, ensuring that our people are always working to push the frontier.

We await the next AI breakthrough as eagerly as anyone, standing ready to shuffle our short-term priorities at any time. We know, however, that our long-term success and impact comes from attention to technical fundamentals and persistent trends.

Most of Temporal’s work is open source—see for yourself here:

What You Will Do

  • Work as a software engineer
  • Maintain and expand a deep understanding of agentic coding
  • Design and build agentic coding systems that we can trust to deliver high-quality outputs
  • Design and implement Temporal AI SDK features supporting a broad variety of frameworks and libraries.
  • Develop a deep understanding of AI application development patterns and techniques, including emerging approaches and architectures.
  • Take end-to-end ownership of new features, working with other teams to deliver exceptional reliability and a great developer experience.
  • Work with multiple programming languages: Python and TypeScript, Java, Go.
  • Serve as a domain expert on AI design patterns, collaborating with field staff to provide best-practices and canonical examples.
  • Work directly with our developer community to debug issues that need expert attention and get feedback on Temporal features and APIs.
  • Write public technical documentation describing Temporal concepts and APIs.
  • Go the extra mile to support a customer in need, on the rare occasion that our teams’ engineering expertise is needed.
  • Travel to meet your coworkers for a week once or twice a year.
  • Attend the occasional developer conference to talk about how great Temporal is (optional).

What You Won’t Do

  • Work as a Data Scientist, Data Analyst, Devops SWE, or SRE.
  • Work in an office (unless you want to, but you’d be by yourself). Temporal is a fully-remote company.
  • Commit code that’s poorly-tested or works “most of the time”. Temporal aspires to be “Reliable as Gravity”, and we expect our code to be the same.
  • Work behind closed doors. Our work is open source—that means PRs and comments are open to the public, too.
  • Sit in meetings all day. We mostly communicate in writing, and use meetings mainly for status updates and thorny issues that need input from the whole group.
  • Wake up to pager alerts. We’re extremely active in supporting our customers and the community, but we don’t do 24/7 on-call.

What You’ll Bring

  • 3+ years of professional work experience and passion for harnessing generative AI, particularly for agents and coding.
  • A deep understanding of how to use AI to increase quality, not only to increase quantity.
  • A sense of taste in code and software development practice. Your approach should be opinionated and thoughtful, but not dogmatic.
  • Fluency in two or more programming languages, and an affinity for learning new ones.
  • Strong experience with concurrent programming—you should know how to use mutexes, atomics, and other concurrency primitives safely.
  • Experience designing APIs and writing documentation for publicly-available libraries or modules.
  • Strong technical communication skills—written and verbal—in English.
  • BS or MS in Computer Science (or a closely-related degree), or equivalent work experience writing production-grade software.

Nice to Have

  • Familiarity with Temporal’s programming model (e.g. you’ve written an app on Temporal).
  • Experience building agents or other AI applications
  • Background in machine learning, model training, data science, or machine learning systems.
  • Experience contributing to the architecture and design of large-scale distributed systems.
  • A track record of open source software contributions, including contributions to 3rd party libraries.
  • Graduate degree in Computer Science.

Compensation

  • The estimated pay range for this role is $160,000 - $200,000.
  • Additionally, this role is eligible to participate in Temporal's equity plan.
Compensation ranges reflect salary and commission compensation (when applicable) across several geographic markets. Employment offers carefully consider multiple factors, including prior experience, knowledge, expertise, skillset, market location, and job level assessed during the interview process.

jobs.description:
We are hiring an Investor Relations Associate to help grow the investor side of Paires, the network of family offices and high-net-worth individuals our founders raise from.

Paires is where founders come to raise capital. We pair them with the right investors from a large, engaged global investor network, then our agents manage the relationships that turn into meetings. It is a two-sided platform, live with paying clients, profitable and self-funded, built by a small, senior, flat team that ships fast.

The role

The craft of this seat is allocator trust, and we are hiring people early in that craft who are already showing they have it. You will work alongside our senior investor team on live mandates: qualifying allocators, preparing briefs, running follow-ups, and keeping investor relationships warm between deals. And from day one you will build your own: identifying family offices and HNWIs who back US startups, earning first conversations, and growing a book that is yours.

You do not need a decade of relationships. You need the beginnings of a real network, a method for growing it that you can explain, and the discipline to treat other people's capital and privacy with care. The rest, the mandate craft, the briefing standard, the judgment calls, you learn here, working next to people who do this every day. One thing this seat is not: technical. Our engineers build the platform and the agents. You work inside them, so your hours go to investors instead of admin.

What you will own

  • Your growing book. The allocator relationships you bring and the ones you open here, qualified and kept warm.

  • Mandate support that matters. Investor qualification, briefing notes, and follow-through on live deals, done to the house standard.

  • New doors. A monthly rhythm of first conversations with family offices and HNWIs who are new to Paires.

  • Your development. Every investor call you shadow and every brief you write compounds into the senior version of this seat.

You are a fit if you

  • Have started building an allocator network for real, through a seat in wealth management, private banking, a family office, placement, or your own hustle, and can show relationships you opened yourself.

  • Can explain your method. How you find the right investors, how you earn the first conversation, and how you stay useful to them after it.

  • Know what your investors actually do with their money, and ideally that includes direct allocations into US startups.

  • Listen more than you pitch. Allocators trust you because you never waste their time, and you would rather lose a meeting than force one.

  • Treat discretion as a reflex. Names, allocations, and conversations stay confidential, always.

  • Work like it's 2026. AI tooling runs your pipeline and prep, so your hours go to people.

What we offer

Fully remote and async. Your day overlaps with US Eastern time for a few hours, not full US hours. Meetings batch on Mondays and Thursdays, the rest is deep work. The best AI tooling, paid. A senior team to learn the craft from, live deal flow from week one, and a seat that grows into managing your own side of the network.

How to apply: hit apply, which takes you to our short application form. We read every application. Do not include investor names anywhere in it. We evaluate composition, not contacts.

Location: 100% Remote (candidate must reside in an approved state: AL, AR, DE, FL, GA, ID, IN, IA, KS, KY, MS, MO, NH, NE, NC, OK, SC, SD, TN, TX, UT, VA, WV, WI)

Company Overview
Glint Tech Solutions is a women-owned, global IT staffing and recruiting firm serving enterprise clients across the USA and Canada.

Project Description
A leading healthcare payer client is seeking a Senior Healthcare Informatics Analyst who will independently provide analytics to understand and improve how healthcare is valued, utilized, and provided. This role develops analytic attributes related to patient-level health utilization/outcomes, provider performance measures, risk-adjusted revenue optimization, medical cost management, and patient/provider engagement behavior, collaborating with business areas and IT to lead problem solving, solution development, and strategic planning.

Key Responsibilities

  • Independently provide analytics to understand and improve how healthcare is valued, utilized, and provided
  • Develop analytic attributes pertaining to patient-level health utilization/outcomes, provider performance measures, and risk-adjusted revenue optimization
  • Support medical cost management and analysis of patient/provider engagement behavior attributes
  • Lead problem solving, solution development, and strategic planning in collaboration with other business areas and IT
  • Ensure compliance with all laws and regulations associated with duties and responsibilities

Mandatory Skills

  • Healthcare experience required, with Medicare Advantage trend analysis experience
  • Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, statistics, economics, analytics, or computer science (4 years of relevant experience may substitute; Master's preferred)
  • 4+ years of healthcare, analytics, IT, or management consulting experience
  • Strong critical thinking, analytical, and problem-solving skills
  • Experience building predictive models
  • Strong knowledge of SQL, SAS, R, Python, Tableau, or similar query/analytic/visualization tools
  • Basic knowledge of the U.S. healthcare delivery system in a payer or provider setting

Nice-to-Have Skills

  • Strong knowledge of outcome research design and controlled study design
  • Advanced knowledge of SAS, including Enterprise Miner
  • Strong understanding of provider payment methodologies, population health management, and risk adjustment
  • Strong understanding of clinical groupers, including episode and risk groupers (DRG, APC, ETG, MEG, DxCG, HCC)
  • Strong understanding of quality metrics (HEDIS, AHRQ)
  • Knowledge of commercial risk optimization and MA risk optimization

jobs.description:
What We Do

We’re on a mission to empower animal healthcare professionals with opportunities to earn more and achieve greater flexibility in their careers and personal lives.

Powered by groundbreaking technology, Roo has built the industry-leading veterinary staffing platform, connecting Veterinarians, Technicians, and Assistants with animal hospitals for relief work and hiring opportunities. Roo empowers the largest network of over 20,000 veterinary professionals to help more than 9,000 animal hospitals provide quality care to more pets.
Together, we’ve provided more than 3 million hours of healthcare, helping Veterinarians earn more than $200 million.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Brand & Integrated Marketing to lead Roo’s brand team and shape how the veterinary community experiences Roo across channels, audiences, and touchpoints.

This role is responsible for leading the team that brings Roo’s brand to life across content, social, community, PR, events, campaigns, web, paid channels, and more. You’ll help create the narratives, creative systems, and signature moments that make Roo’s brand feel clear, cohesive, meaningful, and unmistakably Roo.

You’ll lead a growing brand team across brand/content, social/community, and events, while helping guide external partners across PR, design, web, ads, and other brand programs. You’ll work closely with teams across the business to ensure Roo’s brand shows up thoughtfully, creatively, and consistently across the full customer journey.

Responsibilities

Brand & Campaign Leadership

  • Set the strategic direction for Roo’s brand team, translating business and marketing priorities into focused brand strategies, compelling campaigns, and elevated creative direction.
  • Lead integrated campaigns from audience insight and messaging through creative direction, channel planning, execution, measurement, and iteration.
  • Elevate the quality, clarity, creativity, and visual consistency of Roo’s brand work across major campaigns and everyday touchpoints.
  • Use performance data, audience insights, and campaign learnings to improve how brand work is planned, prioritized, and measured.
  • Grow Roo’s reach across social, community, events, content, and emerging channels.
  • Develop brand-led programs and moments that build stronger connection with vets, techs, hospitals, and the broader veterinary community.
  • Bring creative ideas to new channels, formats, and audience opportunities while keeping Roo’s brand consistent and high-quality.

Thought Leadership & External Storytelling

  • Shape Roo’s brand narrative across core audiences, ensuring our story is clear, credible, and relevant to the veterinary community.
  • Lead thought leadership programs, including industry reports, customer stories, executive visibility, authored content, speaking opportunities, and other high-impact storytelling moments.
  • Partner with PR to support earned media, industry moments, press angles, and proof points that strengthen Roo’s credibility.
  • Conduct ongoing brand and audience research to track awareness, perception, and engagement, and translate insights into stronger messaging and storytelling.
  • Identify opportunities to evolve Roo’s voice, messaging, and market-facing story as our audiences and business goals grow.

Team & Partner Management

  • Lead and develop a growing brand marketing team across brand/content, social/community, and events.
  • Guide the work of external partners across PR, design, web, ads, and other creative needs, ensuring output is aligned to Roo’s strategy, voice, and quality bar.
  • Partner with teams across Roo to bring brand guidance, messaging, and promotional support to customer-facing programs, launches, and moments.
  • Create scalable systems, templates, and ways of working that help the team and company activate the brand consistently.
  • Use AI and emerging tools thoughtfully to improve research, workflow, content development, reporting, and team efficiency while maintaining strong human judgment and Roo’s quality bar.

Qualifications

  • You have experience in brand marketing, integrated marketing, campaign marketing, or a related role, with experience leading multi-channel work from strategy through execution.

  • Facilitate customer discussions alongside internal stakeholders while capturing detailed meeting notes, customer insights, feature requests, and validation outcomes.

jobs.excerpt: OverviewLynker Corporation is a leading provider of innovative solutions in weather and climate science.
jobs.description:
Overview

Lynker Corporation is a leading provider of innovative solutions in weather and climate science. With a commitment to excellence and a passion for innovation, Lynker leverages cutting-edge technologies and scientific expertise to support the creation and delivery of improved operational weather forecasts. As part of our ongoing growth and expansion, we are seeking a dynamic and experienced API Developer to join our growing team.

Responsibilities

Duties of the API Developer will include the following:

  • API development: design and build APIs that ingest structured data and serve results to downstream users and applications.
  • Structured outputs: generate versioned, schema-conformant outputs in multiple formats, including PDF and JSON, that faithfully represent the underlying data.
  • Schemas & versioning: define and maintain output schemas, data contracts, and schema and API versioning, using standards such as OpenAPI and JSON Schema, so consumers can rely on stable interfaces as the system evolves.
  • CLI (secondary): provide a lightweight command-line interface over the same functionality for scripted and batch use.
  • Security & deployment: help package and deploy services soundly, applying good practices for access control, dependency management, and compliance in secure or government-adjacent environments.
  • Testing & validation: write unit and integration tests and output-validation checks to confirm results are correct, well-formed, and reproducible.
  • Documentation & collaboration: document APIs, schemas, and output formats; coordinate with the Science and Platform teams that define the underlying data and logic to keep interfaces clear.

Qualifications

The API Developer selected should have the following:

  • Master's in computer science, software engineering, data science, or a related field; or a Bachelor's plus 1-2 years building APIs, services, or data pipelines; or equivalent practical experience, including military or self-taught paths.
  • Proficiency in at least one modern programming language; Python experience is a plus, as it is the likely production language for this work.
  • Experience designing and consuming REST/JSON APIs and working with structured data formats.
  • Understanding of data schemas and versioning, and why stable data contracts matter to downstream consumers.
  • Comfort with Git, Linux, testing, and command-line workflows.

The Ideal API Developer will have the following:

jobs.excerpt: About KyraKyra is an enterprise influencer marketing platform working with brands like SharkNinja, Coach, H&M, Ray-Ban, and Converse.
jobs.description:
About Kyra

Kyra is an enterprise influencer marketing platform working with brands like SharkNinja, Coach, H&M, Ray-Ban, and Converse. Our platform manages the full lifecycle — creator discovery, campaign management, content review, payments, analytics, and AI-powered intelligence across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.

The Opportunity

You will build Kyra's growth engine from scratch. We run two businesses that feed each other: a profitable managed-service agency that has won enterprise brands for years, and a subscription platform backed by proprietary creator and trend data.

Nobody owns growth across both sides yet, or makes them compound into each other. That is your job. You own the full funnel, run constant experiments, and find the fastest, cheapest ways to win and keep brands. But this is not a traditional growth marketing role, and we are not looking for a traditional marketer. Marketing channels can be learned. What cannot be taught is the instinct to deconstruct a problem, automate the mechanical parts, and build the tools that make one person move like a team.

If you have built a tool, a plugin, a workflow, or an automation that replaced something you used to do by hand — even if you had never written code before — you are who we are looking for. Whatever you did before matters less than how fast you learn and what you build.

Greenfield role with a real budget and a number you own end to end. If you want a clean slate, a live product, and total ownership, read on.

What You'll Do

Own the Number. Active brands is yours: subscribed brands running at least one live campaign in a rolling 30 days. Real usage and real revenue, not vanity signups. For the first 90 days the proxy is qualified leads while you build the pipeline. By year one, active brands is what you answer for.

Build Before You Scale. Before you spend a pound on ads, you build the measurement layer: tracking, dashboards, baselines. None of it exists yet. You instrument the funnel so you know exactly where it leaks, then you fix the leaks before you pour more in. You do not fool yourself with the numbers.

Invent the Channels. There is no channel plan to inherit and no fixed list to run. Paid, organic, lifecycle, AI search, partnerships, things that do not have a name yet — you develop new channels and new ideas, spin up a test in any of them in a day, read the data honestly, and kill what does not work. The mix a year from now should contain things nobody at Kyra has thought of today.

Build the Loop. This is the centre of the role. The agency feeds the platform with warm, high-intent brands. The platform deepens those relationships and frees the agency to win more. Each brand makes the next one cheaper. Build the referral mechanics, the agency-to-platform motion and the data flywheel so growth compounds instead of restarting every quarter.

Build Your Own Tools. This is what separates the role from every other growth job. When you see a repetitive process — ad creative generation, lead scoring, reporting, competitive monitoring — you do not file a ticket with engineering. You sit down with Claude Code or Cursor and build it yourself. A skill that writes ad copy against your brand voice rules. An agent workflow that generates 100 creative variants from a spreadsheet. A pipeline that pulls the data you need into a dashboard every morning. The tools you build are force multipliers. They are how one person moves like a team.

Feed Insight Back into Product. You sit closest to the funnel and the data, so you see what would actually move growth. Surface it. Find the levers inside the product itself: ways to make sharing and referral native, ways to pull more creators in and keep them active, the bits we should change to grow faster. Growth here is as much a product input as a channels job.

What We're Looking For

We would rather hire someone who can learn marketing in months than someone who arrives with a fixed playbook and applies it regardless of fit. The list below reflects that.

Required

  • Builder instinct. You have built at least one internal tool, automation, or workflow that replaced a manual process. We will ask you to walk through how you deconstructed the problem, what you built, and what it saved. This matters more than your channel list.

  • Deep AI proficiency — beyond chat. Not "I use ChatGPT for copy." You build stored, reusable workflows: custom skills, agents, chained tools. You encode your expertise into systems that compound over time. You ship things with Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent, and you know how to orchestrate LLM APIs into pipelines. You treat AI as infrastructure, not an assistant.

  • A track record of moving a number, with the evidence to prove it. Acquisition, conversion, retention, revenue — you have moved a metric yourself, hands on the levers rather than managing from a distance.

  • Fast, honest experimentation. Clean hypotheses and clean A/B tests, with a real grasp of sample size and significance. You scale winners and kill losers without sentiment — including your own ideas.

  • Adaptability. Tools and ways of working change constantly here. You learn new domains and new tools in days, and you would rather work out the right approach than reapply the last one.

  • Spreadsheet modelling. CAC, payback, funnel maths, cohorts.

  • London-based or able to travel in regularly. We want you in and around the team.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Coding — Python or JavaScript to wire systems together and automate the boring parts.

  • SQL, to pull and analyse warehouse data yourself.

  • Paid channel depth (Google, Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn) — budget management, CPL and CPA.

  • B2B, influencer/creator, or two-sided marketplace experience.

  • SEO and AI search optimisation depth.

Traits That Matter

You deconstruct your own workflow before you try to optimise it. Creative. Self-starting. Comfortable with ambiguity. Product-minded as well as channel-minded.

You build the system, not only run it. You form strong hypotheses and kill the weak ones without sentiment. You do not need rigid processes or hand-holding. Tools and ways of working change constantly here, and you thrive on that. A blank page excites you.

What Success Looks Like

Month 3: Measurement layer built from nothing — dashboards, funnels, baselines. Qualified leads pipeline is built and baselined. At least two acquisition experiments are live with clean tracking. You have built at least one tool or automation that made you measurably faster. CAC is baselined and you can already name the biggest leaks.

Year One: Active brands are growing at the agreed run-rate. CAC payback is under 12 months on at least one proven, repeatable channel. Net revenue retention is above target, proving the loops work. You have a ranked view of which channels to scale and which to cut. A growing library of tools and workflows you built that compound your output.

Why This Role

You get ultimate freedom to build, proprietary creator and trend data nobody else has, a two-sided business with real activation levers, and the founders behind you. You build the engine and drive it from day one.

Benefits

🌎 Location: London-based, hybrid. 3 days per week in-office, 4 days during your first two weeks so you get the most out of onboarding and if Europe based then remote but occasional travel to London as part of the role.

🌴 Annual Time Off: 25 days PTO + bank holidays, 4 company-wide days off (Kyra Days), 3 wellness days, and paid sick leave each year.

📚 Growth: Annual Learning & Development budget to invest in your skills.

💰 Rewards: Annual bonus scheme to recognise great work.

🩺 Healthcare coverage for US-based team members.


AI is core to how we operate. Use it to elevate your work. But everything in your application should reflect your own judgement and experience.

💟 Support

If you have a condition or require an adjustment to our interview process - please let us know so we can make adjustments to support you. Please note that when you submit an application or resume, your data will be processed in line with our privacy policy.

We’re looking for a highly organized, detail-oriented Credentialing & Payer Contracting Coordinator to help clinicians move efficiently from onboarding to payer participation and billing readiness.

You’ll collect and maintain provider information, submit applications, follow up with payers, track agreements and effective dates, and ensure every open item reaches a clear resolution.

Wyoming's rural healthcare organizations serve communities surrounded by mountains, high plains, ranchlands, rivers, open roads, and wide-open spaces.

Deep understanding of DAMA_DMBoK, DCAM, and ISO/IEC 38505.

Designing centralized, federated, or hybrid governance models.
Enabling stewardship roles and workflows, being able to align data governance practices to business value and developing use cases for deployment of governance processes including defining data ownership and identifying data owners as well as data stewardship and data stewards.
Has experience in establishing steering committees, RACI matrix for governance and cadence for on-going governance program.

AI Risk & Compliance

Understanding of emerging regulatory frameworks (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF).
Ability to assess AI/ML models for fairness, bias, transparency, and safety.

Knowledge of ethical AI frameworks, transparency requirements, and accountability structures.
Creating policy guardrails for model development and deployment.

The Role

In a consumption-based business, revenue isn't won at contract signature—it's earned every day. That makes Finance a critical strategic partner, sitting at the center of the decisions that drive growth, profitability, and customer success. In this role, you'll work directly with executive leaders to influence pricing, structure complex deals, guide capital allocation, and shape the metrics that define business performance. If you're looking for a role where your insights directly impact company strategy—not just reporting results after the fact—this is it.

The Senior Director of Finance – Consumption Business Partner is a senior finance leadership role within Lumen, serving as the primary finance partner to the Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) for consumption-based revenue and reporting into Business Finance. This is one of the most analytically demanding and commercially influential finance roles in the business: revenue is inherently variable, forecasting is a competitive advantage, and — unlike seat-based SaaS — there is no clean ARR number to anchor the plan. Revenue is a function of what customers actually use.

This position partners closely with the CRO leadership team, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Customer Success, Product Finance, COGS finance and the enterprise consumption-modeling (Data Finance) team to ensure commercial decisions are grounded in sound financial analysis. The role focuses on forecast narrative, pipeline-to-consumption conversion, customer and segment risk & opportunity, deal economics, and go-to-market efficiency — translating enterprise model outputs and usage economics into clear commercial implications, trade-offs, and recommendations.

The overriding objective is to enable better CRO decisions and forecast explainability — on deals, pricing guardrails, and go-to-market investment — by turning complex consumption dynamics into a clear financial narrative and actionable recommendations.

Work Location

This is a work from home position within the U.S.

The Main Responsibilities

Main Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary finance partner to the CRO and CRO leadership team for consumption-based revenue, and act as the finance voice in major commercial decisions.
  • Translate enterprise consumption forecasts and usage economics into commercial insights, forecast narratives, and action plans across segments, customers, pipeline, and go-to-market motions.
  • Provide finance support on pricing guardrails and deal structures without owning enterprise models, product assumptions, or cost foundations.

Forecast Narrative, Planning & Business Reviews

  • Translate enterprise consumption forecasts into CRO forecast narratives and rolling outlooks spanning committed ARR, consumption run rates, draw-down schedules, and overage projections.
  • Lead monthly business reviews (MBRs) with CRO leadership, providing insight into consumption trends, forecast risks, and plan variances.
  • Apply committed-to-consumed revenue bridges to quantify gaps between contractual commitments and expected revenue consumption, and explain key drivers.
  • Analyze the pipeline-to-commitment-to-consumption conversion path, identifying where bookings are strong but consumption is lagging.
  • Partner with Revenue Operations to ensure CRM, usage, and financial data align and support a consistent commercial narrative.

Performance, Customer & Segment Analytics

  • Own customer- and segment-level revenue risk and opportunity analysis, translating usage-health signals into quantified financial impacts.
  • Maintain portfolio health KPIs, including consumption rates, draw-down velocity, overage revenue, usage NRR, consumption churn, and usage-based LTV.
  • Identify early warning signs of consumption risk and quantify revenue impact before churn events occur.
  • Deliver cohort-level analysis on consumption growth, usage contraction, and overage-driven expansion while differentiating structural and seasonal trends.
  • Partner with Customer Success on usage-health scoring and post-sale consumption strategies.

Deal Economics, Pricing & GTM Efficiency

  • Serve as the CRO's finance partner on consumption-based deal structures, including committed-spend floors, overage rates, discount tiers, and draw-down terms.
  • Model the economics of large deals to assess whether commitments align with expected usage.
  • Support pricing-model evaluations, including pure consumption, hybrid, and tiered usage models, along with ASC 606 revenue-recognition considerations.
  • Maintain discount guardrails and approval thresholds in partnership with Sales Operations and Legal.
  • Provide financial insights on GTM efficiency, including CAC payback, usage-driven expansion, seller productivity, and demand-generation ROI.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Leadership

  • Collaborate with Revenue Finance, Product Finance, Data Finance, and COGS teams to maintain a single, integrated financial perspective.
  • Partner with the CRO and HR to design compensation plans and SPIFs that align seller behavior with consumed revenue.
  • Contribute revenue organization insights to executive, senior leadership, and Board materials through enterprise FP&A processes.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor, influencing commercial decisions through data-driven analysis and storytelling.
  • Drive continuous improvement of consumption-finance processes, tools, and analytical capabilities.

What We Look For in a Candidate

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.
  • 12+ years of progressive experience in financial planning and analysis, business finance, or commercial finance, including senior-level business partnering.
  • Direct experience with consumption-, usage-based, or hybrid pricing models, and building or leveraging usage-based revenue forecast models.
  • Prior experience supporting a revenue, sales, or commercial organization (e.g., CRO), including exposure to deal-desk or commercial-finance structures.
  • Strong analytical and financial modeling skills, including dynamic, scenario-based forecasting.
  • Excellent communication and executive presence, with the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders with data-driven insights and translate financial concepts for non-finance audiences.
  • Strong data fluency and experience working with large usage datasets.
  • Solid understanding of ASC 606 revenue recognition, including variable consideration, usage-based contracts, and pre-purchase arrangements.
  • Proficiency with financial systems and tools such as Excel, Power BI, and CRM platforms (e.g., Salesforce).
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, matrixed environment with strong adaptability, collaboration, and results orientation.

Preferred

  • Experience in cloud infrastructure, data platforms, API-first, or other consumption-based businesses.
  • SQL skills and familiarity with usage-data platforms and data warehouses, including Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery.
  • Experience with complex contract structures, including committed spend, overages, and draw-down mechanics.
  • Familiarity with consumption-based sales compensation and quota-attainment models.

At Gardens Interactive, we're building games centered on connection, collective adventure, and emergent stories.   • Plan, recruit, and interview technical roles within the Gameplay Engineering team.

Hands-on Development

  • Review pull requests and unblock engineers on hard technical problems.

  • Debug and resolve complex cross-system issues, especially around multiplayer sync, performance, and stability.

  • Prototype or build out gameplay systems directly when the team needs an extra pair of hands.

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Partner closely with game design, art, and production to scope features and keep engineering aligned with the creative vision.

  • Experience working cross-functionally with design, art, and production in a real production environment.

  • Comfortable operating with high ownership in a lean team where you wear multiple hats.

  • Strong communication skills: able to explain technical trade-offs to non-engineers and rally a small team around a plan.

Nice to Have

  • Experience shipping a live-service or online multiplayer game post-launch (patching, live ops, backend services).

  • Experience at an independent or mid-size studio.

  • Experience with performance profiling and optimization.

The Team

  • Reports to the Technical Director.

  • Leads the Gameplay Engineering team.

  • Partners closely with the Backend Lead, Technical Director, Production, Design, Art, QA, and the broader engineering organization.

How We Work

We believe great games are built by people who care deeply about both the work and one another. Our values guide how we collaborate, solve problems, make decisions, and grow together. They're practical behaviors, not slogans, and they're part of how we hire, give feedback, and support one another every day.

We're looking for teammates who are excited to:

  • Stay curious and ask thoughtful questions.

  • Adapt when plans change.

  • Exercise good judgment rather than chase perfection.

  • Care for the success of the whole team, not just their own work.

  • Pursue ambitious goals while remaining humble enough to keep learning.

  • Commit fully to the shared adventure we're building together.

  • You adapt comfortably when priorities evolve.

  • You balance ambition with pragmatism.

  • You communicate thoughtfully and seek feedback.

  • You care about helping your teammates succeed.

  • You embrace uncertainty as part of creating something new.

jobs.excerpt: We are hiring an Investor Network Manager to grow the investor side of Paires, the network of family offices and high-net-worth individuals our founders raise from.
jobs.description:
We are hiring an Investor Network Manager to grow the investor side of Paires, the network of family offices and high-net-worth individuals our founders raise from.

Paires is where founders come to raise capital. We pair them with the right investors from a large, engaged global investor network, then our agents manage the relationships that turn into meetings. It is a two-sided platform, live with paying clients, profitable and self-funded, built by a small, senior, flat team that ships fast.

The role

The network in your title is the heart of the platform, and your job is to grow it. The craft is allocator trust. You find the right family offices and HNWIs, earn the first conversation, and become the person whose calls get answered within a day. Month after month you open new relationships, match investors to live mandates, brief them properly before every meeting, and keep your book warm through honest work that never pushes.

If you have this craft, you have a book to show for it, and that book will let you contribute in your first weeks here. What Paires adds is everything a lone operator cannot offer their investors: a steady flow of curated opportunities, each one briefed and followed through. Your relationships become more valuable inside the platform, and the ones you build here compound on top. One thing this seat is not: technical. Our engineers build the platform and the agents. You work inside them, so your hours go to investors instead of admin.

What you will own

  • Your book. The allocator relationships you bring, plus the ones you build here, qualified, mapped, and kept active.

  • Growth on two tracks. Warm additions through your circle and referrals, and new allocators you open from scratch, from first touch to first allocation.

  • Mandate matching. The right investors paired with live deals, briefed before every meeting, their feedback captured after.

  • The standard. Your investors answer you within a day because you have earned it.

You are a fit if you

  • Know how to earn an allocator's trust and have done it before, in wealth management, private banking, a family office, placement, or your own advisory practice, and hold an active network of family offices and HNWIs to show for it.

  • Built that book yourself and can do it again. You have a working method for opening allocator relationships from nothing, and your network's origin story proves it.

  • Can contribute early. Your relationships are current and warm enough that mandate-fit allocators will take a call on your word.

  • Know direct deals. Your investors allocate to US startups at the growth stage, wherever in the world those investors sit, and you speak their screening language of thesis, check size, structure, and downside.

  • Qualify honestly. You can tell an allocator who deploys from one who takes polite meetings, and you protect everyone's time accordingly.

  • Treat discretion as a reflex. Names, allocations, and conversations stay confidential, always.

  • Work like it's 2026. You run your pipeline, briefs, and follow-ups inside modern AI tooling, so your hours go to relationships instead of admin.

What we offer

Fully remote and async. Your day overlaps with US Eastern time for a few hours, not full US hours. Meetings batch on Mondays and Thursdays, the rest is deep work. The best AI tooling, paid. A live deal flow your investors will thank you for, and a platform that multiplies what one person with good relationships can do alone.

How to apply: hit apply, which takes you to our short application form. We read every application. Do not include investor names anywhere in it. We evaluate composition, not contacts.

jobs.excerpt: Wyoming Rural Healthcare Finance and Revenue Cycle Leadership OpportunitiesRural Staffing Services partners with rural hospitals, clinics, public hospital districts, and community healthcare organizations throughout Wyoming to identify experienced finance and revenue cycle leaders who understand the unique realities of rural healthcare.
jobs.description:
Wyoming Rural Healthcare Finance and Revenue Cycle Leadership Opportunities

Rural Staffing Services partners with rural hospitals, clinics, public hospital districts, and community healthcare organizations throughout Wyoming to identify experienced finance and revenue cycle leaders who understand the unique realities of rural healthcare.

We are currently connecting with professionals who may be interested in active and upcoming finance, accounting, reimbursement, revenue cycle, billing, coding, and patient financial services leadership opportunities across Wyoming.

These opportunities may include leadership within Critical Access Hospitals, rural and community hospitals, Rural Health Clinics, Federally Qualified Health Centers, public hospital districts, long-term care organizations, and integrated rural healthcare systems.

Explore Rural Healthcare Opportunities at RSSJobs.org

This application may connect you with the specific opportunity you were viewing, as well as other current or upcoming rural healthcare positions throughout Wyoming that align with your experience and goals.

Visit to explore additional rural healthcare opportunities and communities.

This Is More Than a Finance Role

Strong financial and revenue cycle operations help protect healthcare access for an entire rural community.

These leaders ensure organizations can accurately capture revenue, manage resources responsibly, support employees, maintain compliance, and remain financially strong enough to continue caring for the people who depend on them.

In a rural healthcare organization, finance and revenue cycle leaders often work across departments and may have broader responsibilities than they would in a larger system. The strongest leaders understand how registration, coding, billing, reimbursement, patient accounts, accounting, and operational decisions connect to one another.

They are collaborative, detail-oriented, approachable, and able to turn complex financial information into practical guidance for employees, department leaders, executives, and governing boards.

Opportunities May Include

This application may connect you with current or upcoming roles such as:

  • Controller
  • Assistant Controller
  • Finance Director or Manager
  • Accounting Director or Manager
  • Revenue Cycle Director or Manager
  • Patient Financial Services Director or Manager
  • Patient Accounts Manager
  • Business Office Director or Manager
  • Billing Director or Manager
  • Coding Director, Manager, or Supervisor
  • Health Information Management revenue cycle leadership
  • Reimbursement Director or Manager
  • Chargemaster or Charge Description Master leadership
  • Accounts Payable or Accounts Receivable leadership
  • Payroll leadership
  • Senior billing, coding, or patient accounts supervisory roles

What You May Lead

Responsibilities will vary by organization and position and may include:

  • Leading accounting, finance, revenue cycle, billing, coding, or patient financial services functions
  • Supporting accurate and timely financial reporting
  • Managing month-end and year-end close processes
  • Developing budgets, forecasts, and financial performance reports
  • Strengthening billing, collections, cash flow, and reimbursement performance
  • Monitoring key revenue cycle metrics and identifying opportunities for improvement
  • Supporting accurate coding, charge capture, claims submission, and payment posting
  • Overseeing patient accounts, financial counseling, and collection processes
  • Ensuring compliance with payer, regulatory, accounting, and documentation requirements
  • Preparing for financial, coding, billing, or compliance audits
  • Developing policies, procedures, workflows, and internal controls
  • Training and supporting finance and revenue cycle employees
  • Collaborating with clinical, operational, IT, HIM, and executive leaders
  • Helping employees understand how their work affects organizational sustainability
  • Supporting system implementations, process improvements, or departmental restructuring

What You Will Bring

Qualifications will vary by opportunity, but organizations may seek:

  • Progressive experience in healthcare finance, accounting, revenue cycle, billing, coding, reimbursement, or patient financial services
  • Previous leadership experience as a director, manager, controller, supervisor, or comparable leader
  • Knowledge of healthcare reimbursement, payer requirements, billing practices, and financial operations
  • Experience with Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurance, and patient-pay accounts
  • An understanding of hospital, clinic, or healthcare-system workflows
  • Experience analyzing financial or revenue cycle performance and communicating findings to leadership
  • Strong organizational, problem-solving, and team-development skills
  • Experience with Critical Access Hospitals, Rural Health Clinics, FQHCs, public hospital districts, or community healthcare organizations
  • Relevant education or professional credentials based on the position
  • A collaborative and relationship-focused leadership style

Some opportunities may prefer credentials such as CPA, CHFP, CRCR, CPC, CCS, RHIA, RHIT, or other finance, coding, revenue cycle, or health information certifications. Requirements will depend on the specific role.

Why Rural Wyoming?

Wyoming's rural healthcare organizations serve communities surrounded by mountains, high plains, ranchlands, rivers, open roads, and wide-open spaces. These organizations frequently operate with lean teams, limited resources, and a tremendous responsibility to the communities they serve.

Finance and revenue cycle leadership in a rural organization provides the opportunity to see the direct impact of your work. Improving a process, supporting a team, or strengthening reimbursement can help preserve services, protect jobs, and keep care available close to home.

Join the RSS Rural Talent Network

By applying through this page, you are joining the confidential Rural Staffing Services talent network. You may be considered for current or upcoming finance and revenue cycle leadership opportunities that align with your background, goals, location preferences, and availability.

Please include your resume and let us know:

  • Which Wyoming communities or regions you would consider
  • Whether you are open to relocation
  • Whether you are interested in permanent, interim, remote, fractional, or multiple types of opportunities
  • Which areas best match your experience, such as accounting, finance, billing, coding, reimbursement, patient accounts, or full revenue cycle
  • Your experience with rural hospitals, Critical Access Hospitals, public hospital districts, FQHCs, or community healthcare organizations
  • Which position or community you were viewing on RSSJobs.org

Our team personally reviews each application. When we identify an opportunity that may be a strong match, we will contact you directly to share more about the organization, community, responsibilities, and next steps.

Your information will be handled professionally and confidentially.

Visit to explore additional rural healthcare positions, leadership opportunities, and communities throughout Wyoming.

Work Where It Matters.

As the U.S. enters a new capex supercycle across data centers, factories, housing, and renewables, joining PermitFlow means building the AI infrastructure at the core of every construction project driving the next wave of reindustrialization.

We’ve raised over $90M, most recently completing our Series B, from top-tier investors including Accel, Kleiner Perkins, Initialized, Y Combinator, Felicis, and Altos Ventures, with backing from leaders at OpenAI, Google, Procore, ServiceTitan, Zillow, PlanGrid, and Uber.

We're growing fast and the recruiting function needs to scale with us. As Recruiting Operations Manager, you'll partner directly with the Head of People to centralize process, establish standards, and build the infrastructure that keeps our recruiting engine running smoothly as we grow. You'll own the operating layer end to end and make sure recruiters, coordinators, and hiring managers are all working from the same playbook.

This is a role for someone who operates independently, moves quickly, and earns trust fast. You'll proactively identify opportunities and risks, make recommendations, align stakeholders, and execute at a high level without sacrificing accuracy. Strong attention to detail, clear communication, and a real command of change management are core to this role. You'll be a trusted partner to the Head of People and the connective tissue that makes the recruiting function feel seamless to everyone it touches.

This role reports to the Head of People and is based in our NYC office on a hybrid M/W/F schedule.

What You'll Do

  • Own Our Recruiting Systems: Serve as the primary owner and administrator of Ashby; configuring pipelines, building reports, driving adoption of underused features, and integrating with our broader stack (Claude, Fathom, and beyond). You don't just use AI tools; you build with them and ship automations that measurably change how the team operates.

  • Run the Data: Build and maintain the single source of truth for hiring across the company. Own funnel reporting and recruiter capacity models, and partner closely with our People Operations Manager on headcount planning and prioritization. You're skeptical of numbers until you've checked the filters, and you use data to problem-solve and influence decisions at every level of the org.

  • Define How We Operate: Codify ownership across the recruiting function on who closes, who schedules, who owns references and offers, and run weekly priorities + capacity cadence that keeps the team aligned without adding meeting bloat. Document everything, maintain SLAs, and build the rituals that support a smooth and fast paced recruiting engine.

  • Level Up Interview Infrastructure: Extend our gold-standard interview model across the org, launch interviewer training programs, build and maintain interview kits, and keep documentation clean and consistent. Champion structured, bias-mitigated hiring practices through ongoing calibration and education.

  • Navigate Compliance and Immigration: Own the recruiting side of immigration; managing candidate work authorization status, coordinating visa sponsorship timelines with our People Ops team and outside counsel, and ensuring hiring workflows stay compliant. You don't need to be an immigration expert, but you need to know enough to move candidates through without delays or missteps.

  • Drive Offer and Referral Consistency: Own the tooling, templates, and approval workflows that bring consistency and speed to our offer process. jobs.description:
Role Title: Medical Writer / Clinical Document Author

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote

micro1 is engaging Medical Writers / Clinical Document Authors to participate in a customer’s project focused on developing advanced AI-assisted writing tools for clinical documentation. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.

Scope of Work

  1. Author and review realistic evaluation tasks based on Clinical Study Reports, DSURs, PSURs/PBRERs, and related clinical documents to inform AI tool development.
  2. Apply expert judgment to assess whether AI-generated content fulfills clinical template and structural requirements, including ICH E3 organization, section sequencing, cross-referencing, and appendix management.
  3. Evaluate scientific accuracy in narrative sections such as efficacy, safety summaries, discussion, and conclusions, distinguishing true scientific or interpretive errors from stylistic differences.
  4. Trace narrative claims to source records—tables, figures, listings, and protocols—to verify that all assertions are appropriately supported.
  5. Provide clear and structured written rationales for each assessment, enabling precise diagnosis and improvement of AI model behavior.
  6. Collaborate with project leads to refine evaluation frameworks and document best practices for clinical regulatory writing in the context of AI.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Minimum 5 years of regulatory medical writing experience at a sponsor, CRO, or as an independent consultant.
  2. Direct experience independently authoring or leading the authoring of full Clinical Study Reports, beyond summaries or partial contributions.
  3. Fluency with ICH E3 and conventions for periodic safety documentation (ICH E2F, ICH E2C) and eCTD placement.
  4. Demonstrated ability to read and interpret TFLs and protocol documents, identifying where narrative diverges from source data.
  5. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, especially in providing structured, actionable feedback on clinical content.
  6. Advanced degree in life sciences, pharmacy, or medicine (PhD, PharmD, MD, MSc), or equivalent depth of authoring experience.
  7. Experience across multiple clinical phases and therapeutic areas; oncology and haematology expertise is especially valued.

Join our customer's team and leverage your authoring expertise to help design the next generation of AI-assisted clinical documentation solutions. This high-bar role offers you the chance to shape how tomorrow's writing teams draft and review regulatory documents — through your expert input, judgment, and real-world experience.

Staff Accountant

Snapshot of Curvion Blue

Curvion Blue is a high-performance revenue operations and sales augmentation company that helps businesses build, optimize, and scale their revenue engines.

We operate in a fast-moving environment with numerous companies, brands, offers, sales teams, vendors, and revenue relationships moving through our financial systems. Our accounting function needs to be accurate, organized, proactive, and capable of handling complexity at scale.

We're looking for a Staff Accountant who is more than a transaction processor. We need someone who can own day-to-day accounting responsibilities, manage a high volume of financial activity, reconcile complex transactions, accurately administer commissions, and identify issues before they become problems.

Experience in an agency, BPO, outsourced accounting firm, SaaS company, sales organization, marketplace, or another high-volume financial environment is highly preferred.

Position Overview

The Staff Accountant is responsible for maintaining accurate, timely, and well-documented financial records across Curvion Blue's operations.

This role supports a high-volume, multi-company financial environment where billing, revenue, payments, and sales commissions flow across dozens of external companies, brands, offers, and revenue relationships.

The Staff Accountant will own or support core accounting workflows across:

  • Accounts payable

  • Accounts receivable

  • Billing and invoicing

  • Revenue reconciliation

  • Sales commissions

  • Payroll and commission schedules

  • Credit cards and expenses

  • Cash and banking

  • Account reconciliations

  • Month-end close

  • Financial reporting support

The right person is highly organized, analytical, detail-oriented, and comfortable working independently. They should be able to look across large amounts of financial data and quickly identify when something doesn't tie out, doesn't make sense, or doesn't match the underlying agreement.

You should naturally ask:

"What should this number be, and why isn't it?"

rather than simply entering what is in front of you.

You SHOULD Apply If

  • You have experience managing high-volume accounting activity across multiple companies, entities, customers, vendors, or revenue streams.

  • You have experience with sales commissions, variable compensation, or commission reconciliation.

  • You have experience with billing, invoicing, AR, and revenue reconciliation.

  • You are comfortable working with large amounts of transactional data.

  • You have worked in an agency, BPO, outsourced accounting firm, SaaS company, sales organization, marketplace, or other fast-paced environment.

  • You are exceptionally detail-oriented and naturally notice when something doesn't reconcile.

  • You can investigate discrepancies rather than simply flagging them.

  • You can manage recurring deadlines without constant follow-up.

  • You are comfortable working independently in a remote environment.

  • You communicate quickly when something is wrong or when you need additional information.

  • You enjoy improving processes rather than simply following them.

  • You can move quickly without sacrificing accuracy.

You SHOULD NOT Apply If

  • You need someone to give you a checklist for every task.

  • You have only worked in low-volume accounting environments and are uncomfortable with a high volume of transactions.

  • You have little experience with reconciliations or investigating discrepancies.

Editorialist is a luxury fashion and personal styling platform built for ultra-high-net-worth clients in the US market. We manage the full order lifecycle — from procurement and vendor coordination to final delivery — on behalf of clients who expect flawless execution every time. Our operations run 18 hours a day, 7 days a week, across a distributed team spanning multiple countries and time zones.

We’re a small, high-performance team where every person has real ownership and visible impact. You won’t be a cog—you'll be the person who keeps the engine running. We move fast, we document rigorously, and we hold ourselves to standards that match the caliber of clients we serve.

This is a role for someone who finds genuine satisfaction in precision, thrives in a remote-first environment, and wants to grow within an operations function that’s actively scaling.

Role Overview

    The Operations Associate (OA) is central to how we deliver for our clients. In this role, you’ll take end-to-end ownership of the order lifecycle — from procurement through to confirmed delivery — and you’ll take pride in getting it right every time. You hold yourself to a high bar, communicate clearly under pressure, and treat every order as a reflection of the standard we’ve built. You’ll work closely with teams across merchandising, finance, customer experience, and engineering to keep things moving and resolve issues before they become problems.

    Domain: Order Lifecycle Management

    Location: Remote — Based in the Asia Pacific region (India, Philippines, Bangladesh, or similar time zones preferred).

    Working Hours: Shift-based on a 2-week rotating roster (afternoon and night shifts) within the 8:30 AM–1:30 AM UTC window, with 2 rotational days off per week.

    Reporting Structure: Reports to the Assistant Manager of Operations; day-to-day shift guidance provided by Senior Associates

    Experience: 3–5 years in operations, order management, or a related field

Key Responsibilities

    1. Order Lifecycle & Execution

  • Take total ownership of the order journey: procurement, payment verification, vendor communication, and dispatch tracking.

  • Maintain rigorous documentation: real-time, time-stamped notes and mandatory proof uploads (receipts/screenshots).

  • Verify critical data (SKUs, pricing, shipping) to eliminate gaps before final completion.

  • Strictly adhere to defined Service Level Agreements (SLAs) at every stage.

    • 2. Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Proactively identify and resolve bottlenecks across teams — you drive issues to resolution rather than passing them along.

  • Collaborate with the finance team on payment discrepancies and the customer support team on delivery delays.

  • Report system issues to the engineering team with full context so problems get fixed, not just logged.

  • Provide clear, structured shift handovers including a log of active escalations and pending cases.

    • 3. Quality & Compliance

  • Hold yourself to a high standard of accuracy across payment verification and vendor confirmations.

  • Continuously improve your knowledge of our processes and stay current as they evolve.

  • Take feedback seriously and use it to raise your own bar — repeat errors are something you actively work to eliminate.

    • 4. Vendor & Escalation Management

  • Manage vendor relationships and track order SLAs to ensure timely delivery.

  • Attempt first-level resolution on stalled orders before escalating to Senior Associates, with a full summary of actions already taken.

  • Hand off shifts with structured notes so the next associate can pick up seamlessly.

How Success Is Measured

    This is a metrics-driven role. You’ll be measured on accuracy, timeliness, and documentation quality.

    95%+ Accuracy Score & 90%+ Task Error Score within the first 30 days, plus SLA adherence, error rate, and documentation completeness tracked ongoing.

    Days 1–30: Shadow order processing workflows and build foundational accuracy

    Days 31–60: Take on full order processing independently; begin managing internal and external communications

    Days 61–90: Achieve full operational ownership, meet success metrics, and pass the process knowledge assessment with 90%+ accuracy

Who We’re Looking For

  • Experience: 3–5 years in operations, e-commerce order management, logistics, or a closely related field.

  • Detail Orientation: You catch what others miss and find genuine satisfaction in accurate, complete work.

  • Clear Communication: You give concise, data-backed updates and flag issues with context, not just alerts.

  • Ownership Mentality: You don’t consider an order done until it’s successfully fulfilled and documented.

  • Tech Comfort: Comfortable working in order management systems and confident reporting bugs with enough detail for engineering to act on.

  • Availability: Able to commit to shift-based work within the 8:30 AM–1:30 AM UTC window, including rotational weekend coverage.

Nice To Have_

Mindset

Why You’ll Love Life at GotPhoto

Once you have completed your probation, you have the option to work remotely from within Europe for up to 40 days per year. Whether you are visiting family or simply seeking a change of scenery, we support a work-from-anywhere culture that helps you stay inspired.

What Matters to Us

Research shows that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds may refrain from applying for positions if they feel they don't meet all qualifications. We strongly encourage you to apply if you’re interested: we're excited to discover how your distinctive experience can enhance our team!
